title: Rename semantic primitives and synchronize publish pipeline
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: Our Figma library contains mixed naming conventions for primitives (colors, spacing, type, icons) and multiple variant groupings for atomic components. This causes confusion for engineers onboarding the UI kit, repeated mispublishes, and a sizable drift between the canonical UI kit and product branch libraries. Goals: 1) Introduce a clear, semantic primitive naming scheme (semantic-color: bg/fg/muted/interactive, spacing: s-1..s-8, type: body/label/caps) and migrate tokens. 2) Normalize component anatomy so variants are grouped by 'mode' and 'state' using swap-based grouping instead of nested component sets. 3) Apply a grid-first auto-layout standard to all button/table/chart frames so constraints behave predictably when nested. 4) Implement a pre-publish checklist & automated linter to prevent accidental layer renames and orphaned tokens. 5) Coordinate the publish pipeline so product branches receive a single, automated package update with a changelog. Deliverables: migration guide, updated Figma library file, pre-publish linter rule set, and rollout notes for engineering.
acceptance_criteria: All semantic tokens exist with new keys and a one-to-one map to legacy tokens documented in Confluence
Primary button, table row, and chart primitives use grid-first auto-layout and pass visual regression smoke tests at three sizes
Variant grouping pattern implemented: top-level set = mode (primary/secondary/ghost), nested swap = state (default/hover/disabled/focus)
Pre-publish linter flags 100% of renamed token keys in a dry-run on the UI kit file
Publishing automation creates a changelog entry and tags the product branch; no manual file copies required for target repos
design_notes: Prefer semantic keys over platform-specific names (e.g., 'bg-surface' instead of 'gray-100') to make runtime mapping easier for infra
Avoid combining size and state in the same variant axis; use swap components for state transitions to simplify K/V cache sizing heuristics used by engineering
Buttons should be constrained to a 4px grid with explicit min/max width tokens to avoid hugging behavior when used in data tables
Charts: separate 'frame' from 'render layer' so that axis labels keep fixed spacing while the render layer can flex for responsive widths
Tables: canonical row height tokens (s-5 / s-6) and a 'dense' variant implemented as a swap rather than a separate component to preserve structure
implementation_steps: 1) Create 'semantic-primitives-v2' page in the UI kit; add new tokens and a mapping table to legacy keys
2) Run token-migration script in Figma (batch rename plugin) in dry-run mode and export report
3) Update 10 highest-used components (button, input, select, table row, table header, chart frame, toast, badge, tag, nav item) to new primitives on a feature branch
4) Apply grid-first auto-layout constraints and document examples for nested uses
5) Wire up pre-publish linter (Figma plugin config + Node script) and run against the main UI kit file; fix flagged issues
6) Publish new UI kit as 'ui-kit-semantics-2025.3' with changelog and bump product branch dependencies via automation
7) Coordinate with engineering for SDK token mapping and add migration toggle in front-end repo for 2 sprints
risks: Engineers may miss migration mapping if changelog lacks clear transformation examples
Automated linter false positives could block publishing if rules are too strict
Large pulls from product branches during rollout may introduce visual regressions if old tokens remain in product files
Tight coupling between variant structure and runtime assumptions could require minor runtime changes (batching/kv cache sizing)
rollback_plan: If critical regressions are found after publish, revert the UI kit to the pre-release tag, notify teams via #design-system, and coordinate a targeted patch that re-applies semantic keys incrementally (component by component) until safe.
